title: EU AI Act Article 9 Risk Management System -- What High-Risk Providers Must Establish by August 2, 2026
context: 2026-08-27 engine cycle -- Article 9 risk-management duty is binding for Annex III high-risk systems from August 2, 2026
body: EU AI Act Article 9 obliges the provider of a high-risk AI system to establish, implement, document, and maintain a risk management system for the entire lifecycle of that system, and to run it as a continuous, iterative process. For Annex III high-risk systems, this duty binds from August 2, 2026. The risk management system must cover four steps: identify known and reasonably foreseeable risks, estimate and evaluate those risks, adopt appropriate mitigation measures, and run post-market monitoring. The Council of AI maps this directly to measured containment. A risk register that is self-asserted is not evidence; a risk register whose control measurements are independently signed -- a verified measurement credential over each mitigation check -- is. The Council of AI measurement board supplies per-axis evidence that slots into the Article 9 lifecycle loop, so a provider can show an auditor that mitigation is measured rather than merely declared. The honest boundary is monitored containment, not provable isolation: Article 9 requires you to know and watch the risk surface, not to claim the system can never fail. Concretely: (1) instrument each residual-risk control so its state is measured on a schedule. (2) sign each measurement so the Article 9 documentation is auditable end-to-end. (3) feed deviation events into the Council Signal Containment Incident Index for traceability.
